facts.value: Providence and Worcester Railroad Company (PWRR; NASDAQ: PWX), Worcester, Massachusetts; regional freight railroad.
Genesee & Wyoming Inc. (G&W; NYSE: GWR), through its wholly owned subsidiary Pullman Acquisition Sub Inc.

$25.00 per share in cash, without interest. Each preferred share is deemed converted into 100 common shares, with accrued dividends. 53% premium to the $16.30 close on 08/12/2016 (p. 33). Termination fee $3.785 million. Voting agreement with the Eder Trusts (about 17.3% of common, 78.1% of preferred).
DEFM14A definitive proxy statement dated 09/19/2016 (filed 09/20/2016 per the supplied file name).
mixed: Party A's Q4 2015 equity-interest approach prompted the hiring of GHF, and the Board then ran a target-led auction (Q1).

facts.field: Currency and units of bid prices
facts.value: US dollars per share of common stock, assuming conversion of the preferred stock into common. The filing also gives implied equity values in $ millions, which are recorded in Notes.
Greene Holcomb & Fisher LLC (GHF), whose business BMO Capital Markets Corp. acquired on 08/01/2016; BMO delivered the fairness opinion on 08/12/2016.
Hinckley, Allen & Snyder LLP; unnamed STB regulatory counsel.

In Q4 2015 Party A, a Class I rail partner, raised an interest in buying equity in Providence and Worcester, and the Board hired GHF in January 2016. In March 2016 the Board decided to sell. GHF contacted 29 buyers, 25 signed confidentiality agreements, and nine sent IOIs of $17.93–$26.50 per share by 06/01. Seven advanced to management presentations and the data site; late entrant Party C joined in July, and six LOIs of $19.20–$24.00 arrived in late July. On 07/27 the Transaction Committee took G&W and Party B into confirmatory diligence and negotiation, prioritizing Party B at $24.00 from 08/04, while Parties D and E briefly re-engaged and fell away. On 08/12 G&W raised its bid to $25.00 in cash and dropped its CVR, Party B declined to raise, and the Board signed with G&W that day; the deal was announced 08/15/2016.

cells.Question: Process and round map: one process with three rounds?
cells.Recommended answer: Yes. One process. R1: outreach and IOIs (from week of 03/28/2016). R2: management presentations, data site and LOIs for the seven advanced (from 05/23–06/01). R3: definitive negotiation with G&W and Party B (from 07/27). Party C, entering unsolicited in July, belongs to live round 2.
cells.Why, with page: E6: selection plus a distinct information stage opens R2 (p. 29). The LOI round was not announced as final, so the move to confirmatory diligence and negotiation opens R3 (p. 30). R3 is dated 07/27, not 07/22: G&W topped Party E only after its 07/26 revision (pp. 29–30). Gap of about two months or more with no acquirer contact: Party A meeting (Q4 2015, 10/01–12/31/2015) to management meeting with Party A on 03/22/2016 (at least 12 weeks). E5: (a) not met, Party A was kept in view (p. 27); (b) met on duration only, no reported end; (c) met (03/14 decision). So no second process.
cells.What changes if answered differently: Most plausible alternative: treat 07/27 as the end of an Inferred final round 2 with no round 3; rows 35–57 move to round 2 and Rounds loses its third line. Splitting round 2 at the mid-June LOI request has no support (same bidders, same stage).
